properties.name: Cape Bruguieres
properties.region: Murujuga (Dampier Archipelago), Western Australia
properties.what: Submerged lithic artefact scatter in the tidal channel between Cape Bruguieres Island and North Gidley Island: 269 underwater artefacts down to -2.4 m
properties.reference: Benjamin et al. 2020, PLOS ONE 15(7): e0233912
properties.position: Approximate

properties.name: Nusa Penida
properties.region: Southeast of Bali, Indonesia
properties.what: Island on the Wallace Line: the deep Badung Strait separates it from Bali and the Lombok Strait from Lombok
properties.position: Island centre

properties.name: Flemming Cave (Cootamundra Shoals)
properties.image_alt: Dr Nic Flemming in horse-collar scuba gear (pixel portrait)
properties.region: Van Diemen Rise, Timor Sea, 240 km NW of Darwin
properties.what: 1982 Sirius Expedition. A cave and overhanging ledges at about 60 m below the 45-48 m terrace at Buoy Juliet II, east side of Dubbo Mesa
properties.reference: Flemming, N.C. A survey of the late Quaternary landscape of the Cootamundra Shoals, North Australia. 7th International Diving Science Symposium, Padova
properties.position: Juliet II read from Flemming Fig. 6 (about ±1 km). Buoy Alpha on the main shoal is published as 10°50'13" S, 129°13'10" E

properties.name: Madura Strait Homo erectus
properties.image_alt: Homo erectus skull, front view (pixel icon)
properties.region: Madura Strait, north of the port of Surabaya, East Java, Indonesia
properties.what: Two Homo erectus skull fragments and 36 vertebrate species dredged from a drowned Solo River valley in 2014–2015: the first hominin fossils from the seabed of submerged Sundaland. Cut-marked turtle bones and broken bovid bones point to hunting.
properties.depth: Seabed about 20 m below sea level, dredged down to 32 m
properties.reference: Berghuis, H.W.K., Veldkamp, A., Adhityatama, S. et al. 2025. A late Middle Pleistocene lowstand valley of the Solo River on the Madura Strait seabed, geology and age of the first hominin locality of submerged Sundaland. Quaternary Environments and Humans 3: 100042. doi:10.1016/j.qeh.2024.100042
properties.position: Approximate (about ±1 km): centre of the sand extraction area as mapped in Berghuis et al. 2025 (Fig. 1C), between Tanjung Perak port and the Suramadu Bridge

properties.name: Madjedbebe
properties.region: Mirarr country, western Arnhem Land, Northern Territory (about 50 km inland, within the former Jabiluka lease)
properties.what: Sandstone rock shelter with the oldest dated human occupation in Australia: dense stone artefact bands with grindstones, ground ochre, reflective additives and ground-edge hatchet heads
properties.age: Occupation from about 65,000 years ago (OSL dating of the lowest dense artefact band)
properties.reference: Clarkson, C., Jacobs, Z., Marwick, B. et al. 2017. Human occupation of northern Australia by 65,000 years ago. Nature 547: 306–310. doi:10.1038/nature22968
properties.position: Approximate (about ±2 km): 12°30′S 132°53′E, published to the nearest arc-minute

properties.name: Liang Bua
properties.region: Near Ruteng, Manggarai, western Flores, Indonesia
properties.what: Limestone cave where the type specimen of Homo floresiensis (the 'hobbit', LB1) was found in 2003
properties.age: H. floresiensis skeletal remains about 100,000–60,000 years old; stone tools attributed to it about 190,000–50,000 years old
properties.reference: Brown, P., Sutikna, T., Morwood, M.J. et al. 2004. A new small-bodied hominin from the Late Pleistocene of Flores, Indonesia. Nature 431: 1055–1061. doi:10.1038/nature02999 · Sutikna, T., Tocheri, M.W., Morwood, M.J. et al. 2016. Revised stratigraphy and chronology for Homo floresiensis at Liang Bua in Indonesia. Nature 532: 366–369. doi:10.1038/nature17179
properties.position: Cave entrance (about ±200 m)

properties.name: Leang Karampuang
properties.region: Samangki village, Simbang, Maros karst, South Sulawesi, Indonesia
properties.what: Painted scene of human-like figures interacting with a Sulawesi warty pig: the oldest known narrative (story-telling) cave art
properties.age: At least 51,200 years (LA-U-series on overlying calcite)
properties.reference: Oktaviana, A.A., Joannes-Boyau, R., Hakim, B. et al. 2024. Narrative cave art in Indonesia by 51,200 years ago. Nature 631: 814–818. doi:10.1038/s41586-024-07541-7
properties.position: Approximate (about ±5 km): Samangki village; the paper does not publish cave coordinates

properties.name: Liang Metanduno
properties.region: Muna Island, Southeast Sulawesi, Indonesia
properties.what: Hand stencil with deliberately narrowed fingers: the oldest dated rock art known anywhere
properties.age: At least 67,800 years (LA-U-series on overlying calcite, 67.8 ± 3.8 ka)
properties.reference: Oktaviana, A.A., Joannes-Boyau, R., Hakim, B. et al. 2026. Rock art from at least 67,800 years ago in Sulawesi. Nature. doi:10.1038/s41586-025-09968-y
properties.position: Approximate (about ±1 km): 4°53′55″S 122°39′34″E as given in public site listings

properties.name: Jerimalai
properties.region: Near Tutuala, Lautém, eastern tip of Timor-Leste (75 m above sea level, under 1 km from the coast)
properties.what: Limestone shelter with the earliest evidence of pelagic (deep-water) fishing, including tuna, and one of the oldest known fish hooks, made from shell
properties.age: Pelagic fish from about 42,000 years ago; shell fish hook about 23,000–16,000 years old
properties.reference: O'Connor, S., Ono, R. & Clarkson, C. 2011. Pelagic fishing at 42,000 years before the present and the maritime skills of modern humans. Science 334: 1117–1121. doi:10.1126/science.1207703
properties.position: Approximate (about ±500 m): 8°23′38″S 127°16′06″E

properties.name: Goulburn Islands crossing
properties.region: Between North and South Goulburn Islands, western Arnhem Land, NT
properties.what: Stories of a narrow strip of land that once joined South Goulburn (Warruwi) and North Goulburn (Weyra) Islands. In one, a fisherman cut down a big paperbark tree that fell into the water and flooded the connection; others credit supernatural beings
properties.depth: Crossing on foot needs sea level 17–20 m lower than present
properties.age: 8890–9680 cal BP (latest time the story could have been valid)
properties.reference: Nunn, P.D. & Reid, N.J. 2016. Aboriginal memories of inundation of the Australian coast dating from more than 7000 years ago. Australian Geographer 47(1): 11–47. doi:10.1080/00049182.2015.1077539 (p. 27, Tables 1–2)
properties.position: Approximate (about ±5 km): the channel between the islands

properties.name: Drowned islands off North Goulburn
properties.region: About 20 km east of North Goulburn Island, NT
properties.what: The submerged islands of Wulurunbu and Lingardji, known to the Goulburn Islands people, identified as a shoal about 20 km east of North Goulburn Island (after Cooke & Armstrong 1998)
properties.age: Not dated separately by Nunn & Reid
properties.reference: Nunn, P.D. & Reid, N.J. 2016. Aboriginal memories of inundation of the Australian coast dating from more than 7000 years ago. Australian Geographer 47(1): 11–47. doi:10.1080/00049182.2015.1077539 (p. 27)
properties.position: Schematic (about ±10 km): '20 km east of North Goulburn Island'

properties.name: Elcho Island crossing
properties.region: Between mainland Arnhem Land and Elcho Island (Galiwin'ku), NT
properties.what: Yolŋu traditions of how Elcho became an island: Djankawu tripped and thrust his walking stick into the sand, 'causing the sea to rush in', and the Ancestresses 'made a long sand-bar' that lasted only until they had crossed
properties.depth: 5 m lower allows a crossing; 10 m lower gives a complete land connection
properties.age: 7450–9140 cal BP (latest time the story could have been valid)
properties.reference: Nunn, P.D. & Reid, N.J. 2016. Aboriginal memories of inundation of the Australian coast dating from more than 7000 years ago. Australian Geographer 47(1): 11–47. doi:10.1080/00049182.2015.1077539 (p. 27, Tables 1–2)
properties.position: Approximate (about ±10 km): south end of Elcho Island

properties.name: Entrance Island crossing
properties.region: Entrance Island, mouth of the Liverpool River at Maningrida, NT
properties.what: Tradition of a submerged crossing at Entrance Island / Maningrida (Cooke & Armstrong 2014, as summarised by McCarthy et al. 2022)
properties.reference: Cooke, P. & Armstrong, G. 2014, cited in McCarthy, J., Wiseman, C., Woo, K. et al. 2022. Beneath the Top End: a regional assessment of submerged archaeological potential in the Northern Territory, Australia. Australian Archaeology 88(1): 65–83. doi:10.1080/03122417.2021.1960248
properties.position: Approximate (about ±3 km)

properties.name: Marchinbar submerged rockshelter
properties.region: North end of Marchinbar Island, Wessel Islands, NT (Golpa Country)
properties.what: Golpa Traditional Owners identified a submerged rockshelter during 2018 fieldwork with Daryl Wesley. A seabed depression, possibly a cave or rockshelter, seen in a Wessel Islands marine survey matched a place known from oral tradition
properties.reference: McCarthy, J., Wiseman, C., Woo, K. et al. 2022. Beneath the Top End: a regional assessment of submerged archaeological potential in the Northern Territory, Australia. Australian Archaeology 88(1): 65–83. doi:10.1080/03122417.2021.1960248
properties.position: Deliberately approximate (about ±10 km): north end of Marchinbar Island; no exact location is published

properties.name: Palaeo-Lake Carpentaria
properties.region: Gulf of Carpentaria
properties.what: Large freshwater lake on the exposed Sahul shelf at lower sea levels, reaching about 190,000 km² at 14 ka. Rising seas breached the Arafura Sill about 11.7 ka, turning it brackish and then marine
properties.age: About 70–12.2 ka as a lake; marine from about 11.7 ka
properties.reference: McCarthy, J., Wiseman, C., Woo, K. et al. 2022. Beneath the Top End: a regional assessment of submerged archaeological potential in the Northern Territory, Australia. Australian Archaeology 88(1): 65–83. doi:10.1080/03122417.2021.1960248 (after Reeves et al. 2008; Yokoyama et al. 2001; Sloss et al. 2018)
properties.position: Lake centre (schematic)

properties.name: Vanderlin Island
properties.region: Sir Edward Pellew Group, southwest Gulf of Carpentaria, NT (Yanyuwa Country)
properties.what: Oldest dated occupation in the Gulf islands, soon after the rising sea reached the area
properties.reference: McCarthy, J., Wiseman, C., Woo, K. et al. 2022. Beneath the Top End: a regional assessment of submerged archaeological potential in the Northern Territory, Australia. Australian Archaeology 88(1): 65–83. doi:10.1080/03122417.2021.1960248 (after Sim & Wallis 2008; Brockwell et al. 2009)
properties.position: Island centre (about ±10 km)

properties.name: Pama-Nyungan origin
properties.region: South of the Gulf of Carpentaria, near Burketown, Queensland
properties.what: Modelled homeland of the Pama-Nyungan language family, which later spread across most of Australia
properties.age: About 6 ka (5.7 ka in Bouckaert et al. 2018)
properties.reference: Bouckaert, R.R., Bowern, C. & Atkinson, Q.D. 2018. The origin and expansion of Pama–Nyungan languages across Australia. Nature Ecology & Evolution 2: 741–749. doi:10.1038/s41559-018-0489-3 · McCarthy, J., Wiseman, C., Woo, K. et al. 2022. Beneath the Top End: a regional assessment of submerged archaeological potential in the Northern Territory, Australia. Australian Archaeology 88(1): 65–83. doi:10.1080/03122417.2021.1960248
properties.position: Schematic: Burketown, standing for the modelled origin area

properties.name: Wellesley Islands
properties.region: Southern Gulf of Carpentaria, Queensland (Mornington Island group)
properties.what: Accounts of a time when the Wellesley Islands were part of a mainland peninsula, until the 'seagull woman' Garnguur dragged her raft back and forth across its neck and it was submerged, forming the islands
properties.depth: About 5 m lower joins the islands to the mainland; 10 m lower gives substantial connections
properties.age: 7450–9140 cal BP (latest time the story could have been valid)
properties.reference: Nunn, P.D. & Reid, N.J. 2016. Aboriginal memories of inundation of the Australian coast dating from more than 7000 years ago. Australian Geographer 47(1): 11–47. doi:10.1080/00049182.2015.1077539 (p. 26, Tables 1–2)
properties.position: Island group centre (about ±20 km)

properties.name: Cape Don (Aragaládi)
properties.region: Cape Don, western tip of the Cobourg Peninsula, NT
properties.what: Tradition of Aragaládi, a submerged island the ancestors came from. A sacred rock was knocked, 'rain fell for a long time there in the middle of the sea … then that place went underwater', and only those with canoes reached the mainland at Cape Don
properties.age: 7930–9520 cal BP (latest time the story could have been valid)
properties.reference: Nunn, P.D. & Reid, N.J. 2016. Aboriginal memories of inundation of the Australian coast dating from more than 7000 years ago. Australian Geographer 47(1): 11–47. doi:10.1080/00049182.2015.1077539 (pp. 27–28, Tables 1–2)
properties.position: Pin at Cape Don; the location of Aragaládi itself is unknown

properties.name: Tiwi crossing (Vernon Islands)
properties.region: Clarence Strait, between the mainland and Melville Island, NT
properties.what: Tiwi story of Mudangkala, an old blind woman who crawled across the land with water following her, forming Clarence Strait and Apsley Strait. Read as a memory of crossing from the mainland via the Vernon Islands before the sea rose
properties.depth: About 12 m lower for a crossing without watercraft; 20 m lower for an easy one
properties.age: 8210–9680 cal BP (latest time the story could have been valid)
properties.reference: Nunn, P.D. & Reid, N.J. 2016. Aboriginal memories of inundation of the Australian coast dating from more than 7000 years ago. Australian Geographer 47(1): 11–47. doi:10.1080/00049182.2015.1077539 (pp. 28–29, Tables 1–2)
properties.position: Vernon Islands (about ±5 km)

properties.name: Brue Reef (Juljinabur)
properties.region: Off the Dampier Peninsula, Kimberley, WA (Bardi and Jawi Country)
properties.what: Bardi and Jawi stories of Juljinabur, now a reef awash at high tide, as an inhabited island that later sank. Nunn & Reid estimate it could have supported 10–100 people
properties.depth: 4 m lower possible; 10 m lower more convincing
properties.age: 7250–9140 cal BP (latest time the story could have been valid)
properties.reference: Nunn, P.D. & Reid, N.J. 2016. Aboriginal memories of inundation of the Australian coast dating from more than 7000 years ago. Australian Geographer 47(1): 11–47. doi:10.1080/00049182.2015.1077539 (pp. 29–30, Tables 1–2)
properties.position: Approximate (about ±5 km): Museums Victoria georeference for Brue Reef
